issue.title: BUG: HDFStore.select evaluates `a | b in <long list>` as an AND
issue.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.

### Reproducible Example

```python
import os
import tempfile

import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": range(10), "b": range(10)})
vals = list(range(100, 140)) + [2]  # 41 values, more than 31

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    path = os.path.join(tmp, "store.h5")
    with pd.HDFStore(path, mode="w") as store:
        store.append("x", df, format="table", data_columns=True)
        got = store.select("x", "a > 7 | b in vals")["a"].tolist()
        small = vals[-21:]
        got_small = store.select("x", "a > 7 | b in small")["a"].tolist()

expected = df[(df["a"] > 7) | df["b"].isin(vals)]["a"].tolist()
print("select 'a > 7 | b in vals' (41 values):", got)
print("same query with 21 values:            ", got_small)
print("expected:                             ", expected)
```

### Issue Description

In a `where` string, an OR whose one branch is an `in` with more than 31 values returns only the rows that match both branches. `"a > 7 | b in vals"` with 41 values returns no rows, while the same frame in memory gives `[2, 8, 9]`. With 21 values the result is right. The reversed order `"b in vals | a > 7"` and `"a > 7 | index in big"` behave the same. Nothing is raised or warned.

Output on 3.0.6 (tables 3.11.1, numexpr 2.14.2):

```
select 'a > 7 | b in vals' (41 values): []
same query with 21 values:             [2, 8, 9]
expected:                              [2, 8, 9]
```

`BinOp.prune` in `pandas/core/computation/pytables.py` (144-181 at 03e5d938ad, from 0.13.0) builds the table condition and the post-read filter separately. An `in` with more than `_max_selectors` values (31, line 117) makes `ConditionBinOp.evaluate` return None (460) so that the term goes to the filter instead, and the inner `pr` (146-149) then returns whichever side is not None. For an OR this leaves the other branch as the condition and the `in` term as the filter, and `read` in `pandas/io/pytables.py` (5297-5298) applies the filter on top of the condition, which is an AND. This is a different path from #17567 / #66162, which was about the filter being dropped when combined with a condition.

In `pr`, when the operator is `|` and one side pruned to None, returning None for the whole OR would send it to the filter as one unit. Raising the existing "too many values" style error would also be better than rewriting the query.

I ran this on pandas 3.0.6. I have not run it on a main build, but the code cited above is unchanged on main at 03e5d938ad.

### Expected Behavior

`store.select("x", "a > 7 | b in vals")` returns `[2, 8, 9]`, the same as the 21-value case and as `df[(df.a > 7) | df.b.isin(vals)]`.
